# Same-course transport across 2013 terms

Use only the earlier study's OULAD 2013 training cohort. Split 2013B learners by parity of the first SHA256 identifier byte. Fit the original day-zero logistic features on even learners and use odd learners to estimate group-specific multiplicative risk corrections (observed withdrawals plus five divided by expected withdrawals plus five). Apply each course's two corrections to probabilities in 2013J, clipping at one. Include courses present in both terms. The matched ablation pools the calibration courses. Within each course preserve original score order in each group. Enumerate prefix-feasible splits of floor(10% of enrollment) seats and maximize minimum group expected recall from corrected risks, subject to losing at most 0.01 original expected captures per seat versus the best feasible split. Break ties by original expected capture then fewer female seats. Compare all six frozen upstream policies on identical input. Report realized pooled minimum group recall and precision, membership differences and paired percentile intervals (5000 within-course learner resamples, seed 1701). Require binding membership change and positive lower recall bounds against every comparator plus precision lower bound at least -0.01 against unrestricted. Report effect sizes for practical interpretation. This exploratory design precedes evaluation and reuses public development data.
